::: {.hero}
# Weather & TTC Delays
A JSC370 final project by Xiran Yin — exploring how 12 years of Toronto weather data predict subway delays using machine learning and natural language processing.
:::

## Project Overview

The Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) carries over **one million daily riders**, making subway reliability a critical piece of urban infrastructure. This project asks a simple but practical question: **can daily weather conditions predict how badly the subway will be delayed?** And if so, **which weather features matter most**?

Using **4,384 daily observations from 2014–2025**, this project integrates three independent data sources — historical weather records, TTC subway delay logs, and rider posts from Reddit's `r/TTC` — to:

1. **Quantify** the statistical relationship between weather and total daily delay duration through regression and Generalized Additive Models (GAM).
2. **Predict** delay severity using three supervised machine learning models (Linear/Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost), evaluated under both regression and classification framings.
3. **Validate** model findings against rider sentiment using VADER sentiment analysis and LDA topic modelling on social media discourse.

## Key Findings (Highlights)

::: {.card-container}

::: {.card}
### Weather matters — but non-linearly
Snowfall has roughly **10× the per-unit delay impact** of liquid precipitation. The precipitation–delay relationship plateaus near 15 mm/day, and temperature effects are **U-shaped** (delays rise at both freezing and extreme heat).
:::

::: {.card}
### XGBoost wins
Among three machine learning models, **XGBoost achieves the best performance** for both regression (RMSE ≈ 84 min, R² ≈ 0.18) and classification (ROC-AUC ≈ 0.74) of severe delay days. Random Forest is a close second; linear models lag substantially.
:::

::: {.card}
### Top predictors
Feature importance analysis ranks **snowfall**, **mean temperature**, and **day-of-week** as the strongest predictors of severe delay days — consistent with both the GAM smooths and the OLS coefficient signs.
:::

::: {.card}
### Riders agree
Independent NLP analysis of `r/TTC` posts shows that sentiment drops sharply on high-delay days, and infrastructure-related complaints (Topic 3) carry the most negative VADER scores — qualitatively triangulating the quantitative findings.
:::

:::

## Data Sources

| Source | Coverage | Access |
|:-------|:---------|:-------|
| [Open-Meteo Historical Weather API](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api) | Toronto daily weather, 2014-01-01 to 2026-01-01 | Free public API |
| [Toronto Open Data — TTC Subway Delays](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/ttc-subway-delay-data/) | Every recorded subway delay 2014–2025 | CKAN API |
| [Reddit `r/TTC`](https://www.reddit.com/r/TTC/) | ~100 recent rider posts mentioning "delay" | Reddit JSON API (cached in `data/`) |

## Reproducibility

The full project is reproducible from a single command. Clone the repository and run:

```bash
quarto render
```

This will re-fetch the weather and TTC data from their public APIs, load cached Reddit posts, fit all models, and rebuild the website. See the [README](https://github.com/xiran-yin/JSC370-finalproject/blob/main/README.md) for setup instructions.
